function: Multi-task transformer predicting precoder parameters (power and dual variables for sum-rate, virtual uplink powers for max-min SINR) and one-step channel prediction, using in-context demonstration pairs (p. 4-6, 8).
system: Single-cell downlink MU-MISO-OFDM: 16-antenna UPA BS (4x4), K=4 single-antenna users, 2.4 GHz, 8.64 MHz with 48 subcarriers, users moving 10-100 km/h, no RIS (p. 3, 8).
method: Decoder-only LLaMA-style causal transformer (4 layers, 512 dim) trained from scratch, multi-task, in-context learning; supervised on WMMSE/Schubert-Boche labels and channel ground truth, MSE/NMSE loss (p. 7-9).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa generator, 3GPP UMa NLOS, 21 clusters x 20 paths, 2.4 GHz; 80,000 training and 10,000 test samples per task; labels from WMMSE and Schubert-Boche (p. 8).
test_conditions: Trained at SNR 0/10/20/30 dB and velocities 10/40/70/100 km/h; tested also at unseen SNR 5/15/25 dB and velocities 20/30/50 km/h, with l=4 in-context demonstrations (p. 9-10).
baselines: Precoding: WMMSE, Schubert-Boche (non-learned), CNN-based BNN [11] matched and fixed (learned). Prediction: LLM4CP [20] (learned) and outdated CSI (p. 9-10).
metrics: Sum rate (bps/Hz) versus SNR, minimum user rate versus SNR, channel prediction NMSE versus velocity, effect of the number of in-context demonstrations (p. 9-11).
q1_support: p. 8: "we utilize the QuaDRiGa channel generator [40]" and "We specifically adopt the 3GPP Urban Macro (UMa) channel model"; the parameters "align with this standard [30]", which is 3GPP TR 38.901.
q2_support: p. 10: "trained using datasets generated at specific user velocities of {10, 40, 70, 100} km/h" and tested at "intermediate velocities (e.g., 20, 30, 50 km/h) that were unseen during the training phase". The unseen SNR points of p. 9 are an SNR sweep and would not count alone.
q3_support: p. 9: "we employ the classical WMMSE algorithm [41] and a CNN-based Beamforming Neural Network (BNN) [11]", compared on sum rate (Fig. 9); p. 10: "we employ the LLM4CP model [20]" and "we include the Outdated CSI scheme", compared on NMSE (Fig. 11).
q4_support: p. 9: "the model employs 4 layers, 4 attention heads, an embedding dimension of 512, and a FFN dimension of 1024" is the only size information; no parameter count, operations or runtime is reported, and p. 11 lists "enhancing its computational efficiency for edge deployment through model compression" as future work.
q5_support: p. 8: "The training dataset and test dataset respectively contain 80000 and 10000 samples for each task", generated with QuaDRiGa and labeled with WMMSE and Schubert-Boche; no link to code or data is given, and QuaDRiGa is a generator, not a released dataset.
notes: Included, area 3 judged by the main metric: one model handles precoding (P1 sum rate, P2 max-min SINR; Figs. 9, 10, 12, 13) and channel prediction (P3 NMSE; Figs. 11, 14); area 2 would apply if channel prediction were taken as the main task. q1=1: QuaDRiGa with the 3GPP UMa model. q2=1 rests on the unseen velocities (p. 10), plus in-context demonstrations drawn from the new condition; the unseen SNR points alone would not count. q3=1: non-learned WMMSE, Schubert-Boche and outdated CSI, plus learned BNN [11] and LLM4CP [20]. q4=0: no parameter count, operations or runtime. q5=0: self-generated data, no link.
